operations.name: Blank Receiving Inspection
operations.setup_note: Support the bought annealed ring on the inspection bench and verify material certification, incoming profile, outside diameter, existing bore and axial width. Confirm that the supplier-provided profile carries the specified machining allowance.

operations.name: CNC Turn – Datum and Hub Side
operations.setup_note: Grip the annealed ring on the gear-side supplier register in bored soft jaws, leaving the datum-side hub accessible; establish face A and prefinish the existing bore as provisional datum B. Complete accessible hub features, the left disc surface and datum-side recesses, retaining hard-finishing stock in the central bore.

operations.name: CNC Turn – Gear Side
operations.setup_note: Reverse onto a low-distortion mandrel locating in provisional bore B and seating against datum A. Finish the gear-side face, gear blank diameter, right bore step and remaining face recesses without removing the central-bore hard-finishing allowance.

operations.name: Machined Blank Inspection
operations.setup_note: Locate the soft machined blank from face A and provisional bore B. Verify turning dimensions, recess profiles, gear and spline blank diameters, and retained bore stock before releasing the blank to hobbing.

operations.name: Hob External Gear and Spline
operations.setup_note: Mount the soft blank on an arbor locating in provisional bore B against face A, retaining the same clamping for both hob tools. Hob the 46-tooth right-hand helical gear and 34-tooth external spline using qualified tooling and settings for the specified tooth profile, lead and crown requirements.

operations.name: Tooth Entry Chamfer and Deburr
operations.setup_note: Locate the hobbed soft part from provisional bore B and face A, with access to the specified gear and spline entry edges. Form the tooth-entry treatments and remove machining burrs before carburizing, preserving every designated do-not-break corner.

operations.name: Continuous Carburize and Integral Quench
operations.setup_note: Load the soft, deburred rings into continuous-carburizer carriers for carburizing and integral quench, targeting 1.2 mm effective case depth and 60–62 HRC after temper. Run the 100-piece order through qualified carrier loads rather than assuming one load; charge per verified finished kilogram, not furnace hours.

operations.name: Temper
operations.setup_note: Transfer the as-quenched rings promptly into qualified tempering loads using suitable support carriers. Low-temperature temper to the required 60–62 HRC without softening the case for subsequent machining.

operations.name: Hardness and Effective Case Verification
operations.setup_note: Support representative tempered parts and a qualified co-processed witness coupon or sacrificial sample for metallurgical inspection. Verify 60–62 HRC surface hardness and 1.2 mm effective case depth with allowance for subsequent bore finishing.

operations.name: Shot Blast – Quench Scale Removal
operations.setup_note: Support the hardened rings on a controlled blast fixture that exposes scaled surfaces without damaging the finished tooth edges. Remove quench scale before hard boring; this is cleaning by blasting, not shot peening.

operations.name: Hard Turn – Datum Bore
operations.setup_note: Hold the hardened gear in a low-distortion chuck with protected contact pads, seat against datum A and indicate the existing bore axis before cutting. Hard-bore datum B to final size and the starred Ra 0.8 finish while holding its perpendicularity to A; leave the nonqualifying faces and bore steps as soft-turned.

operations.name: Final Wash
operations.setup_note: Rack the hard-finished rings so the bore, relief grooves and face recesses drain freely. Remove blast media, hard-turning debris and coolant using a validated cleaning cycle for JDS-G169 Class 6.6.

operations.name: Gear and Spline Inspection
operations.setup_note: Mount the cleaned, hardened part from final bore B against face A using the gear inspection fixture. Check gear and spline tooth size, the specified load-side helix slope, crown and profile deviations, and the applicable spline functional measurements.

operations.name: Final Dimensional and Cleanliness Inspection
operations.setup_note: Locate the finished part in the approved A–B datum fixture and establish the spline datum simulator where required by the clarified controls. Verify dimensions, face and recess profiles, bore perpendicularity, surface finishes and documented JDS-G169 Class 6.6 cleanliness.

operations.name: Part Identification
operations.setup_note: Support the accepted hardened part in a protective nest and apply identification in the approved nonfunctional location. Keep marking away from datum contacts and functional teeth, and preserve the cleaned condition.

operations.name: Rust Preventive and Pack
operations.setup_note: Handle the accepted rings in a clean packing station and apply compatible rust preventive. Pack with separators protecting the gear teeth, spline entries and datum surfaces while maintaining the specified cleanliness.

clarifications.question: What is the confirmed reference diameter for the 3° tapered hub F03?
clarifications.suggested_default: Use the extracted Ø68 basic provisionally for planning only; confirm the diameter before machining.

What is the side-fit tooth-thickness acceptance specification for external spline F02?
clarifications.suggested_default: Do not use the 3.1 reference tooth width as an acceptance limit.

clarifications.question: What is the tooth-thickness acceptance specification for helical gear F01?
Which physical edges are identified by the drawing's DO NOT BREAK CORNER instruction?
What is the datum-side versus gear-side placement of the numbered circular edge treatments?
clarifications.suggested_default: Provisionally place F09, F11, F12 and F13 in the datum-side setup, and F10 and F22 in the gear-side setup; verify against the dimensioned section before release.

clarifications.question: What is the intended datum reference for the F02 position control currently shown as referencing C(M), when datum C is also assigned to F02?
clarifications.suggested_default: Treat C as the spline's functional datum axis for planning, but hold acceptance of the apparently self-referenced position control pending confirmation.

clarifications.question: Where may the part-identification mark be applied?
clarifications.suggested_default: Use an approved nonfunctional axial area away from datum contacts, tooth flanks and specified finish zones.

assumptions.text: Stock is a bought annealed ring with 2.5 mm machining allowance per side: OD 130.2539 mm, minimum bore 39.037 mm and axial width 43.7 mm. The supplier provides the underlying stepped/profiled blank; these envelope dimensions do not represent a solid slug to be hollowed out.
The VMC step from the external-gear sequence is omitted because all supplied production features are rotational or tooth features; no off-axis pocket or component hole requires milling.
Feature descriptions establish datum A on F20 and datum B on F29 despite the incomplete geometry datum entries. Their soft-machined versions are used provisionally before heat treatment.
F19 and F29 are duplicate representations of the same Ø44.037 central bore, not separate bore diameters; they therefore share boring sub-operations.

Finish zones follow their descriptive physical surfaces: F21 is on the datum-B bore, F26 is on the left datum face, F27 is on the right end face, and F24 covers the two disc faces. The right F24 zone is taken to coincide with the F25 face.

The F15 groove instances are provisionally accessible with the datum-side hub features, while F28 recess instances are distributed between the two axial setups. Final instance placement must be checked against the dimensioned axial section.
F28 annular face recesses are lathe face-grooving features represented by groove_od using suitable face-grooving tooling, not VMC pockets.
The drawing-derived gear-table root diameter range of 116.1931–116.5929 mm takes precedence over the assumed 114.0039 mm root diameter in F01.

Both tooth systems remain hobbed. Qualified soft-hobbing tooling and settings must deliver the specified final tooth modifications; the conditional RES 10024 grinding-burn note does not require tooth grinding or grinding-burn inspection when no grinding is performed.

The small F14 and F18 shoulder radii are produced incidentally by the associated turning tools. The F31 and F32 spline-entry radii are formed by the profiled tooth-entry chamfer tooling rather than by separate turning operations.

The confirmed customer instruction requires in-house continuous carburizing with integral quench, followed immediately by temper, to 60–62 HRC and 1.2 mm effective case depth. Heat treatment remains in scope despite the silent drawing.

Leave 0.2–0.3 mm diametrical stock on the central bore during soft turning. Its 0.026 mm size band and Ra 0.8 zone require post-quench hard boring; the other faces and ±0.1 mm bore steps remain soft-turned, with no routine post-HT face cutting or grinding.
Post-temper material_hardness_hrc of 61 represents the midpoint of the specified 60–62 HRC range, not a measured result. As-quenched hardness before temper is unspecified.

Finished weight is estimated at 1.354 kg, not the partial 2.0648 kg. Overall length 38.7 mm splits into a 17.7 mm hub and a 21 mm gear. The bore is Ø50 × 4.5, Ø45 × 5.2, and Ø44.037 × 29. The gear is solid from the bore to Ø68, a web from Ø68 to Ø108 at 8 mm (21 minus 6.5 mm each side), then the rim to root 116.393, plus 63.0 percent of the tooth annulus out to tip 125.254. The hub is a 3 degree taper from Ø66.145 to Ø68, with half the spline annulus Ø55.8 to Ø62.3 removed over 8.7 mm.
F05 with F06/F07 describes cutter-reference geometry, and F30 is an inspection pin rather than a component hole; none is manufactured on the part.
General edge breaking and all deburring are completed before carburizing. The hard-boring pass terminates into the pre-machined entry treatment without a separate post-HT deburr operation.
